sentences.text: JUDGMENT Heard Sri Raja Raghavendra Naik, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Praveena Y.Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1/State.
Though respondent No.2 served remained absent.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
The appellant herein was working as Junior Lineman. He stated to have obtained the job by producing a false caste certificate.
The complainant after having suspected that he obtained government job fraudulently, insisted the authority to verify the genuinity of the caste certificate.
The authority i.e. the Caste Verification Committee verified the caste certificate and opined that the appellant is not belongs to scheduled caste.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant herein preferred an appeal before the Appellate Authority against the said order.
In the meantime, the Caste NC: 2024:KHC-D:9712 Verification Committee directed the officers to lodge a complaint against the appellant herein.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant approached this Court seeking anticipatory bail.
3. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant has not committed any offence.
The entire family members obtained the certificate as 'Bhovi'.

However, due to some inadvertent mistake, the school records of the appellant are shown as 'Bhoweru' instead of 'Bhovi'.
4.
It is further submitted that the appellant belongs to 'Bhovi' community and it comes under the scheduled caste category.
Merely because of the mistake made by the authority, the appellant herein is not responsible for the said act.
Since the matter is pending for consideration before the Appellate Authority, it is not appropriate to register a criminal case against the appellant.

Hence, he may be Bhovi Basavaraja S/O Bhovi ... vs State Of Karnataka on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151173948/
2 enlarged on bail by imposing suitable conditions.

sentences.text: Making such submissions, the learned counsel for the appellant prays to allow the appeal.

5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader filed objections along with copy of Caste Verification Committee NC: 2024:KHC-D:9712 and submitted that the appellant has produced fake caste certificate and obtained job though he is not belongs to the said scheduled caste.
The appeal filed by the appellant deserves to be dismissed.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the findings of the Caste Verification Committee and also order of the Trial Court, it appears from the record that some of the family members obtained the certificate as 'Bhoweru' and others have obtained certificate as 'Bhovi'.
There might be some error by the elders of the family and moreover, whether the appellant has committed the said offence or not is required to be investigated by the Investigating Officer.
Instead of keeping the appellant in dark, it is appropriate to grant him bail and direct him to appear before the jurisdictional police for necessary investigation.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed.

The appellant is ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No.52/2024 of NC: 2024:KHC-D:9712 respondent/police station, on executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with one surety for the likesum, subject to the following conditions:
a) The appellant shall appear before the I.O. within one month from today and shall execute personal bond and also furnish surety.
b) The appellant shall co-operate with the investigation as and when it is required.
